question: Can the President fire a Fed governor?
answer: Only for cause, and only after notice and a chance to respond. On June 29, 2026 the Supreme Court (5-4) kept Governor Lisa Cook in office, holding that courts can review the 'cause' and that she got no notice or hearing. On October 7 the President set up a committee to try again, with a hearing set for November 5, 2026.

items.title: Trump v. Cook — SCOTUS No. 25A312; below D.D.C. and D.C. Circuit
items.text: May the President immediately remove a sitting Fed Governor "for cause," without notice and a chance to answer — and is the Governor's tenure protection constitutional?
kv: Stay denied 2026-06-29 (Roberts for a 5-4 majority): courts may review 'cause', a removal needs notice and a chance to respond, and Cook stays in office while the case continues. On 2026-10-07 the President named a committee to decide whether cause exists; its hearing is set for 2026-11-05.
One Governor's chair is one FOMC vote — and the ruling drew the constitutional fence around the Fed itself: the one agency the removal revolution doesn't reach.

items.title: Trump v. Slaughter — SCOTUS No. 25-332; below D.D.C.
items.text: Does the FTC's for-cause removal protection survive Article II?
kv: Reversed 6–3 on 2026-06-29: FTC protection unconstitutional; Humphrey's Executor no longer shields the modern commission. The Fed was expressly treated as a distinct historical arrangement.
Every independent financial commission except the Fed is now removable at will — the President's hand reaches SEC-style bodies, and only the central bank keeps its carve-out.

rows.what: White House sets up a committee to decide whether there is cause to remove Governor Cook
rows.detail: A presidential memorandum dated October 7 (posted October 8; published in the Federal Register on October 14 at 91 FR 65435) sets up a three-member committee (the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, the Chairman of the EEOC and the Director of the Office of Government Ethics) to review the mortgage allegations and report on whether there is cause to remove Cook, with a closed hearing set for November 5, 2026. It cites Trump v. Cook, 146 S. Ct. 2234 (2026), for the cause standard.

rows.what: Scheduled: White House committee hearing on Governor Cook
rows.detail: Closed, in-person hearing at the White House, at which Cook 'shall appear at the hearing and be examined by the Committee.'

uncertain: The Court did not fully define 'cause' or decide whether Cook can be removed on the facts.

research.title: Federal Reserve Appointment Removal Succession
research.answer: No single personnel chain: five overlapping chains (Article II, regional corporate, FOMC, internal management, oversight/IG); no actor controls every chain.

research.title: The court cases deciding who gets inside the money system
research.answer: A map of 72 case families and 159 dated events on who can hold a Fed account, which agencies survive and how far emergency money powers reach. So far the courts mostly leave gatekeeping power with the Fed, Treasury and bank receivers.
